subject: HEALTH
title: Health 5
description: Grade 5 health education aligned to the 2008 California Health Education Content Standards, which focus fifth grade on Growth and Development, Nutrition and Physical Activity, and Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs, with supporting Personal and Community Health (hygiene, sleep, dental care). Students study body systems, nutrition labels and fitness, healthy body image and media literacy, then a seven-week puberty unit covering hormones, the reproductive systems, menstruation and emotional changes (parents preview materials and may opt out, consistent with CA Education Code). The year closes with tobacco, vaping, alcohol, cannabis and medicine safety, refusal skills, and a health-advocacy campaign.
framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards (Grade 5: Growth and Development; Nutrition and Physical Activity; Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs; plus Personal and Community Health); 2019 CA Health Education Framework

standards.H-5.1.1.N: Describe the food groups, key nutrients and the Dietary Guidelines recommendations for a growing body.
standards.H-5.1.2.N: Explain the importance of limiting added sugars, sodium and saturated fat.
standards.H-5.1.3.N: Describe the components of physical fitness and the benefits of 60 minutes of daily physical activity.
standards.H-5.1.4.N: Explain the relationship between food intake, physical activity, growth and healthy body weight.
standards.H-5.1.5.N: Recognize that healthy bodies come in many shapes and sizes and describe the dangers of unhealthy dieting.
standards.H-5.2.1.N: Analyze how media, advertising, peers and culture influence food choices, physical activity and body image.
standards.H-5.3.1.N: Use Nutrition Facts labels and valid sources to access accurate nutrition and fitness information.
standards.H-5.4.1.N: Use effective communication to express needs for healthy food and physical activity.
standards.H-5.5.1.N: Use a decision-making process to choose healthy meals, snacks and beverages.
standards.H-5.6.1.N: Set and track a goal to improve eating habits or physical activity.
standards.H-5.7.1.N: Plan healthy meals and snacks and a weekly physical activity schedule.
standards.H-5.8.1.N: Advocate for healthy eating and physical activity at home and in the community.
standards.H-5.1.1.G: Describe how body systems (endocrine, circulatory, skeletal, muscular, reproductive) work together and change as people grow.
standards.H-5.1.2.G: Describe the physical, social and emotional changes that occur during puberty.
standards.H-5.1.3.G: Explain the role of hormones and the endocrine system in puberty.
standards.H-5.1.4.G: Identify the structures and functions of the male and female reproductive systems.
standards.H-5.1.5.G: Explain menstruation, nocturnal emissions and other normal pubertal changes.
standards.H-5.1.6.G: Recognize that the timing of puberty varies and that each person grows at their own rate.
standards.H-5.1.7.G: Explain why personal hygiene becomes more important during puberty.
standards.H-5.2.1.G: Analyze how media, family and peers influence feelings about growth, body image and gender roles.
standards.H-5.3.1.G: Identify trusted adults and valid sources of information about puberty and growth.
standards.H-5.4.1.G: Demonstrate how to talk with a parent/guardian or trusted adult about puberty and personal concerns.
standards.H-5.5.1.G: Use a decision-making process to solve problems related to growth, hygiene and changing friendships.
standards.H-5.7.1.G: Practice personal hygiene and self-care routines appropriate to puberty.
standards.H-5.8.1.G: Support others and show respect for individual differences in growth and development.
standards.H-5.1.1.P: Describe hygiene practices for skin, hair, teeth and body odor, including care during puberty.
standards.H-5.1.2.P: Explain the importance of adequate sleep (9–12 hours) and regular dental and medical check-ups.
standards.H-5.7.1.P: Develop and follow a daily personal health routine (hygiene, sleep, dental care).
standards.H-5.1.1.A: Describe the short- and long-term effects of alcohol on the brain and body, including impaired judgment.
standards.H-5.1.2.A: Describe the effects of tobacco and nicotine, including e-cigarettes/vaping and secondhand smoke and aerosol.
standards.H-5.1.3.A: Describe the effects of cannabis (marijuana) and inhalants on the developing brain and body.
standards.H-5.1.4.A: Distinguish between the safe use and misuse of prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
standards.H-5.1.5.A: Explain addiction and why young people's developing brains are especially vulnerable.
standards.H-5.1.6.A: Recognize that most young people do not use alcohol, tobacco, cannabis or other drugs.
standards.H-5.2.1.A: Analyze how advertising, media, flavors and packaging promote alcohol, tobacco and vaping products.
standards.H-5.2.2.A: Explain how family, peers and community norms influence decisions about alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-5.3.1.A: Identify trusted adults and community resources for help with alcohol, tobacco and other drug concerns.
standards.H-5.4.1.A: Demonstrate refusal and negotiation skills to avoid alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-5.5.1.A: Use a decision-making process in situations involving alcohol, tobacco and other drugs.
standards.H-5.6.1.A: Set a personal goal to remain alcohol-, tobacco- and drug-free.
standards.H-5.8.1.A: Encourage others to be alcohol-, tobacco- and drug-free.

resources.name: KidsHealth for Kids
resources.note: Kid-friendly articles on puberty, hygiene, nutrition, fitness and drugs

resources.name: AMAZE
resources.note: Free, medically accurate animated videos on puberty and growing up, with parent guides

resources.name: MyPlate Kids
resources.note: USDA food group guides, activity sheets and games

resources.name: FDA – Tobacco Public Health Education
resources.note: Facts on tobacco, nicotine and vaping

resources.name: NIDA – Parents & Educators
resources.note: Science-based lessons on alcohol, cannabis and other drugs

units.title: Health Skills and Body Systems
units.big_idea: Healthy choices are skills we practice, and our body systems work together as we grow.

units.title: Nutrition for Growing Bodies
units.big_idea: A growing body needs balanced nutrients and fewer added sugars, sodium and saturated fats.

units.title: Physical Activity and Fitness
units.big_idea: Daily activity builds every component of fitness and supports healthy growth.

units.title: Body Image and Media
units.big_idea: Healthy bodies come in many shapes and sizes; media images are often not real.

units.title: Personal Health and Hygiene
units.big_idea: Daily hygiene, sleep and check-ups keep a changing body healthy.

units.title: Puberty: Growth and Development
units.big_idea: Puberty is a normal stage of growth that happens to everyone at their own pace.

units.title: Tobacco, Nicotine and Vaping
units.big_idea: Nicotine is addictive, and tobacco and vaping products harm the lungs, heart and brain.

units.title: Alcohol, Cannabis, Inhalants and Medicines
units.big_idea: Alcohol and other drugs affect the developing brain; medicines are safe only when used correctly.

units.title: Influences, Refusal and Decisions
units.big_idea: Recognizing pressure and practicing refusal skills helps us stay drug-free.

units.title: Advocacy and Year Review
units.big_idea: We can use what we know to help family and friends make healthy choices.

weeks.topic: Health skills and the wellness triangle
objectives: Describe physical, mental/emotional and social health

days.title: Wellness triangle
days.work: Draw a wellness triangle and list three current habits on each side; star the strongest side.

days.title: Eight health skills
days.work: Read a one-page list of the eight CA health skills (access info, analyze influences, communicate, decide, set goals, practice, advocate) and match each to a real-life example.

days.title: Decision steps
days.work: Learn a 5-step decision model (state the problem, list options, weigh consequences, decide, evaluate) and apply it to a bedtime vs. video-game scenario.

days.title: SMART goal
days.work: Write one SMART health goal for the first month (e.g., drink water instead of soda at lunch 5 days a week) and make a tracking chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain the wellness triangle and decision steps to a parent and complete a 6-question quick check.

weeks.assessment: Quick check and SMART goal chart.

objectives: Explain how systems cooperate during exercise and growth

days.title: Body map
days.work: Trace your body on butcher paper and sketch the skeletal, muscular and circulatory systems with labels.

days.title: Heart and lungs
days.work: Take your resting pulse, do 2 minutes of jumping jacks, retake it and explain how the circulatory and respiratory systems responded.

days.title: Nervous system
days.work: Do a ruler-drop reaction-time test 5 times and record results; write how brain, nerves and muscles worked together.

days.title: Endocrine system
days.work: Read a KidsHealth article on glands and hormones and add the pituitary, thyroid and adrenal glands to your body map.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Use the body map to explain to family how three systems work together when you run; complete a labeling quiz.

weeks.topic: Growing and changing; reliable health information
objectives: Describe how bodies grow from childhood to adolescence
Evaluate the reliability of health sources

days.title: Growth timeline
days.work: Make a timeline of your own growth using family photos and recorded heights, and note skills gained at each stage.

days.title: Life cycle
days.work: Compare stages of the human life cycle (infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, older adulthood) in a 5-column chart.

days.title: Is it reliable?
days.work: Compare a .gov health page, a product ad and a social-media post on the same topic using a 4-question reliability checklist.

days.title: Trusted adults
days.work: List at least four trusted adults and two valid sources you could use for health questions and discuss with a parent.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a source-sorting activity (reliable/unreliable) and write a paragraph on how you will check health information.

weeks.topic: Nutrients and MyPlate for a growing body
objectives: Name the six nutrients and their jobs
Describe MyPlate amounts for a 10–11 year old

days.title: Six nutrients
days.work: Make a 6-panel chart of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water with each job and two food sources.

days.title: Nutrients for growth
days.work: Read about calcium, iron and protein needs during growth spurts and list foods rich in each.

days.title: MyPlate check
days.work: Use MyPlate Kids to find daily food-group amounts for your age and activity level and record them.

days.title: Plate collage
days.work: Cut magazine pictures to build a balanced MyPlate collage that meets the recommended amounts.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer a 10-question nutrients quiz and explain your collage to a family member.

weeks.topic: Added sugars, sodium and saturated fat
objectives: Explain why to limit added sugars, sodium and saturated fat

days.title: Sugar in drinks
days.work: Measure the teaspoons of sugar in 5 drinks (soda, juice, sports drink, chocolate milk, water) from their labels and display them with sugar or sand.

days.title: Sodium hunt
days.work: Compare sodium on labels of canned soup, chips, crackers and fresh vegetables and rank them.

days.title: Fats
days.work: Sort food cards into mostly unsaturated vs. saturated fat sources and explain why plant oils and nuts are better choices.

days.title: 5/20 rule
days.work: Learn the 5% low / 20% high Daily Value rule and apply it to 4 pantry labels.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a label-reading worksheet and write three swaps that cut added sugar or sodium.

objectives: Use each part of a Nutrition Facts label

days.title: Label anatomy
days.work: Label every part of a Nutrition Facts panel on a printout and define each in your own words.

days.title: Serving size test
days.work: Pour your usual cereal, measure it, and compare it to the label's serving size; recalculate sugar for your real portion.

days.title: Ingredient lists
days.work: Read ingredient lists in order of weight and identify whole grains and different names for sugar.

days.title: Cereal compare
days.work: Compare 5 cereals for fiber, added sugar and sodium and use the decision steps to choose the healthiest.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a label-reading test using two unfamiliar products.

objectives: Choose water and milk over sugary drinks

days.title: Breakfast matters
days.work: Read a short article on breakfast and concentration, then plan three quick balanced breakfasts.

days.title: Snack sorting
days.work: Sort 20 snack cards into everyday vs. sometimes foods and explain your reasoning with nutrients.

days.title: Make a snack
days.work: Prepare a yogurt parfait or veggie-and-hummus plate with adult help and record its food groups.

days.title: Hydration
days.work: Track your water intake for a day and design a water-bottle reminder chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a one-week healthy snack menu and justify three choices using label data.

objectives: Plan a balanced day of meals

days.title: Food log
days.work: Log everything you eat and drink for one day by food group.

days.title: Analyze the log
days.work: Compare your log with MyPlate recommendations and highlight food groups that were over or under.

days.title: Plan a day
days.work: Plan breakfast, lunch, dinner and two snacks for one day that meet MyPlate amounts within a set budget using grocery flyers.

days.title: Cook a meal
days.work: Help prepare one planned meal with an adult, practicing handwashing and safe knife use.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the meal plan and complete the Nutrition unit test.

weeks.assessment: Meal plan presentation and unit test.

objectives: Define the five health-related components of fitness

days.title: Five components
days.work: Learn the five health-related components of fitness and match an activity to each.

days.title: Endurance test
days.work: Time a 10-minute walk/run and record distance and heart rate.

days.title: Strength tests
days.work: Count curl-ups and push-ups in 30 seconds each and record them.

days.title: Flexibility test
days.work: Do a sit-and-reach test with a yardstick on a box and record the best of three.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Chart your baselines and write one fitness goal for each component.

objectives: Explain benefits of activity for body and mind

days.title: Activity benefits
days.work: Read about how activity helps the heart, bones, sleep and mood, and list five benefits.

days.title: Moderate vs. vigorous
days.work: Try walking, jumping rope and dancing for 3 minutes each and use the talk test to classify intensity.

days.title: Weekly plan
days.work: Create a 7-day plan with at least 60 minutes daily including muscle- and bone-strengthening activity 3 days.

days.title: Screen time swap
days.work: Track screen time for a day and plan two active swaps.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Follow day one of your plan and complete a short quiz on activity guidelines.

objectives: Ask for active options at home

days.title: Ask for activity
days.work: Role-play asking a parent for a family walk or park trip using a clear, respectful request.

days.title: Exercise safety
days.work: List safety rules for heat, hydration, sun and protective gear; check your own helmet fit.

days.title: Family challenge
days.work: Design a one-week family activity challenge with a points chart.

days.title: Retest
days.work: Retest one fitness baseline from week 9 and compare results.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a reflection on your activity goal progress and pass a fitness-unit quiz.

days.title: What is body image?
days.work: Discuss what body image means and write three things your body lets you do that you appreciate.

days.title: Many shapes and sizes
days.work: Look at family photos to see how genetics shapes body type and list factors that affect size.

days.title: Dieting dangers
days.work: Read a KidsHealth article on dieting and list why skipping meals or fad diets harm growing kids.

days.title: Kind words
days.work: Practice replacing body-shaming comments with respectful statements in 5 scenario cards.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on healthy body image and answer a 5-question check.

days.title: Ad techniques
days.work: Learn 6 advertising techniques (bandwagon, celebrity, fun, health claims, giveaways, beautiful people) and find examples in magazines.

days.title: Edited images
days.work: Watch a short before-and-after photo-retouching video and discuss how it affects body image.

days.title: Food ads
days.work: Analyze two kids' food commercials: target audience, techniques and what they leave out.

days.title: Gender messages
days.work: Compare toy or clothing ads aimed at boys vs. girls and note stereotypes about how bodies should look.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create a counter-ad that promotes healthy body image or a healthy food honestly.

objectives: Explain why sweat and oil increase with growth

days.title: Sweat and oil
days.work: Learn how sweat and oil glands become more active in puberty and why body odor and acne happen.

days.title: Skin care
days.work: Read about gentle face washing and acne myths; write a simple morning and evening skin routine.

days.title: Deodorant vs. antiperspirant
days.work: Compare product labels for deodorant and antiperspirant and explain the difference.

days.title: Hair and nails
days.work: Learn how often to wash hair as it gets oilier and practice nail care.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Build a personal hygiene checklist and complete a hygiene myth-or-fact quiz.

objectives: Explain the purpose of dental and medical check-ups

days.title: Plaque check
days.work: Use a disclosing tablet or grape juice to see plaque, then brush for two minutes and recheck.

days.title: Flossing
days.work: Practice flossing technique and explain how sugar and plaque cause cavities.

days.title: Check-ups
days.work: Interview a parent about your last dental and medical check-up and list what was checked.

days.title: Orthodontics and sports
days.work: Read about braces and mouth guards and when they are needed.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create a dental care poster and answer 5 questions on oral health.

weeks.topic: Sleep and a daily health routine
objectives: Explain why growing bodies need 9–12 hours of sleep

days.title: Why sleep?
days.work: Read about sleep and growth hormone, memory and mood, and list four effects of too little sleep.

days.title: Sleep log
days.work: Start a 4-night sleep log with bedtime, wake time and screen-off time.

days.title: Wind-down plan
days.work: Design a 30-minute screen-free bedtime routine.

days.title: Daily routine
days.work: Combine hygiene, dental care, sleep and activity into a daily health routine chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Analyze your sleep log, set a sleep goal and take the Personal Health unit quiz.

weeks.topic: Introduction to puberty (parent notification and opt-out honored)
objectives: Recognize that puberty is normal and timing varies

days.title: Family kickoff
days.work: Parent reviews the unit outline and materials together with the student; set up an anonymous question box.

days.title: What is puberty?
days.work: Watch an AMAZE.org video on puberty and list changes that happen to everyone.

days.title: Different timelines
days.work: Read about how puberty can start between ages 8 and 14 and write why comparing yourself to friends isn't useful.

days.title: Growth spurts
days.work: Graph your height over the past few years and learn about growth spurts and growing pains.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer questions from the question box with a parent and complete a 5-question check.

objectives: Explain how the pituitary gland starts puberty

days.title: Messengers
days.work: Learn how hormones act as chemical messengers and model it with a message-passing game.

days.title: Pituitary gland
days.work: Add the pituitary gland to your body map and explain how it signals the ovaries or testes.

days.title: Hormone effects
days.work: Make a cause-and-effect chart linking estrogen and testosterone to body changes.

days.title: Mood and hormones
days.work: Read about how hormones can affect moods and brainstorm healthy ways to handle mood swings.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw a flowchart of the endocrine system's role in puberty and take a quiz.

objectives: Identify structures of the female reproductive system
Identify structures of the male reproductive system

days.title: Correct names
days.work: Learn medically accurate names for body parts and why using them matters for health and safety.

days.title: Female system
days.work: Label a diagram of the female reproductive system and write the function of each structure.

days.title: Male system
days.work: Label a diagram of the male reproductive system and write the function of each structure.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Create a T-chart comparing changes in both systems during puberty.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a diagram-labeling quiz and submit any questions to the question box.

objectives: Explain erections and nocturnal emissions as normal

days.title: Menstrual cycle
days.work: Watch an AMAZE video and draw a simple 28-day cycle diagram with labels.

days.title: Period supplies
days.work: Learn about pads, tampons and period underwear, and pack a period-preparedness kit list.

days.title: Male changes
days.work: Read about voice changes, erections and nocturnal emissions as normal parts of puberty.

days.title: Hygiene connection
days.work: Write a hygiene plan for managing periods or sweat, odor and shaving.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer a myth-or-fact quiz on puberty changes and discuss with a parent.

objectives: Practice handling changing friendships and crushes

days.title: Feelings wheel
days.work: Use a feelings wheel to name emotions common in puberty and write about one.

days.title: Changing friendships
days.work: Read two scenarios about friends drifting apart and use the decision steps to solve them.

days.title: Crushes and respect
days.work: Discuss crushes as normal and list ways to treat others respectfully, including respecting 'no'.

days.title: Gender stereotypes
days.work: Sort statements about how boys and girls 'should' act into stereotypes vs. facts and discuss respect for all.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a journal entry on a coping strategy for emotional changes and complete a check.

objectives: Communicate about puberty with a parent or trusted adult

days.title: Conversation starters
days.work: Write three conversation starters for talking with a parent about puberty.

days.title: Practice talk
days.work: Have a 10-minute conversation with a parent or guardian using a starter and record one thing you learned.

days.title: Valid sources
days.work: Compare KidsHealth, AMAZE and a random video comment on a puberty question and judge reliability.

days.title: Body autonomy
days.work: Learn about personal boundaries, safe and unsafe touch, and how to tell a trusted adult.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a pocket card listing trusted adults and valid sources and complete a role-play check.

weeks.topic: Puberty review and respect for differences
objectives: Summarize physical, emotional and social changes
Show respect for differences in development

days.title: Concept map
days.work: Build a concept map linking hormones, physical changes, emotions, hygiene and trusted adults.

days.title: Stop teasing
days.work: Role-play responding to teasing about early or late development.

days.title: Self-care kit
days.work: Assemble or list a personal self-care kit for school or travel.

days.title: Advice column
days.work: Write answers to three advice-column questions from fictional 5th graders about puberty.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Growth and Development unit test and discuss results with a parent.

objectives: Describe effects of tobacco on the body

days.title: What's in a cigarette
days.work: Read about nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide and label a body diagram with their effects.

days.title: Straw breathing
days.work: Jog in place 1 minute, then breathe through a thin straw for 30 seconds to simulate damaged lungs; write a reflection.

days.title: Addiction and the brain
days.work: Learn how nicotine changes the brain's reward system and why teens get addicted faster.

days.title: Secondhand smoke
days.work: Research secondhand smoke effects and CA smoke-free laws.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a tobacco-effects quiz.

days.title: What is a vape?
days.work: Read the FDA fact sheet on e-cigarettes and list what is in vape aerosol.

days.title: Myth vs. fact
days.work: Sort 10 vaping statements (e.g., 'it's just water vapor') into myths and facts with evidence.

days.title: Flavors and packaging
days.work: Analyze images of vape packaging and explain how flavors and colors target young people.

days.title: Real norms
days.work: Read survey data showing most youth do not vape and make a bar graph.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a short public service announcement correcting one vaping myth.

days.title: Historic ads
days.work: Compare historical cigarette ads with today's vape marketing and identify persuasion techniques.

days.title: Refusal steps
days.work: Learn refusal strategies: say no clearly, give a reason, suggest an alternative, walk away.

days.title: Role-play
days.work: Role-play 4 scenarios refusing a vape from an older kid or friend.

days.title: Assertive vs. passive
days.work: Practice assertive body language and tone compared with passive and aggressive responses.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform a refusal role-play for a parent and take the tobacco unit test.

objectives: Describe effects of alcohol on the brain and body

days.title: Alcohol pathway
days.work: Trace alcohol's path through the body on a diagram and note effects on the brain, liver and stomach.

days.title: Coordination demo
days.work: Try simple tasks (walking a line, tossing a ball) while spinning first to model impaired coordination, then discuss.

days.title: Developing brain
days.work: Read about why alcohol is especially harmful to the developing brain and why the legal age is 21.

days.title: Short vs. long term
days.work: Make a chart of short- and long-term effects of alcohol.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete an alcohol facts quiz.

objectives: Describe the effects of cannabis on young people

days.title: Cannabis facts
days.work: Read a NIDA for kids article on marijuana and list effects on memory, learning and reaction time.

days.title: Edibles danger
days.work: Learn why cannabis edibles can look like candy and what to do if you find one.

days.title: Inhalants
days.work: Read warning labels on household products and explain why sniffing them can cause sudden death.

days.title: Laws and norms
days.work: Learn that cannabis is illegal under 21 in CA and review data showing most youth don't use it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a matching quiz on cannabis and inhalant effects.

days.title: Rx vs. OTC
days.work: Compare a prescription label and an OTC Drug Facts label and identify each part.

days.title: Dosage math
days.work: Use a Drug Facts chart to find the correct dose by age and weight in 3 practice problems.

days.title: Misuse
days.work: Discuss why sharing prescriptions or taking extra doses is dangerous.

days.title: Safe storage
days.work: Inspect your home's medicine storage with a parent and learn the Poison Control number (1-800-222-1222).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a medicine-safety scenario quiz.

objectives: Explain how to help someone affected by substance use

days.title: Who can help?
days.work: List trusted adults and community resources (doctor, school counselor, Poison Control, faith leader) for drug concerns.

days.title: Family affected
days.work: Read a story about a family member's alcohol problem and discuss feelings and where kids can get support.

days.title: Help script
days.work: Write a script for telling a trusted adult you found a vape or pills.

days.title: Resource card
days.work: Design a wallet-size resource card with key numbers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Alcohol and Other Drugs unit test.

days.title: Influence web
days.work: Make a web of influences (family, friends, media, culture, community) on decisions about drugs.

days.title: Peer pressure types
days.work: Identify spoken, unspoken and online peer pressure in 6 scenarios.

days.title: Alcohol ads
days.work: Analyze an alcohol advertisement for target audience and hidden messages.

days.title: Protective factors
days.work: List protective factors in your life (family rules, activities, goals) and how they help.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph analyzing the strongest influence on you and how to respond.

objectives: Apply the decision process to ATOD scenarios

days.title: Values
days.work: Rank personal values and explain how they guide decisions about drugs.

days.title: Decision chart 1
days.work: Use the decision chart for a sleepover scenario where someone brings alcohol.

days.title: Decision chart 2
days.work: Use the decision chart for a scenario involving a friend's prescription pills.

days.title: Negotiation
days.work: Practice negotiating a safe alternative activity with a friend.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a decision-making assessment with a new scenario.

days.title: Drug-free goal
days.work: Write a personal drug-free goal with reasons and supports.

days.title: Refusal toolbox
days.work: Practice 6 refusal strategies (broken record, humor, change subject, leave, give facts, suggest alternative).

days.title: Record a skit
days.work: Write and record a 1-minute refusal skit.

days.title: Coping without drugs
days.work: List healthy ways to deal with stress, boredom and sadness.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform a refusal skill demonstration scored with a rubric.

days.title: Choose a topic
days.work: Pick a topic (drug-free, vaping myths, healthy drinks, daily activity) and state a clear health-enhancing message.

days.title: Research
days.work: Gather 3 facts from valid sources to support the message.

days.title: Audience
days.work: Identify the audience (younger siblings, family, community group) and plan how to reach them.

days.title: Draft materials
days.work: Draft a poster, brochure or short video script.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Peer- or parent-review the draft with an advocacy checklist.

days.title: Final product
days.work: Create the final poster, brochure or video.

days.title: Call to action
days.work: Add a clear call to action and a source list.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse a 3-minute presentation of the campaign.

days.title: Goal check
days.work: Review your nutrition, activity and drug-free goals from the year and record progress.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present a dress rehearsal to a parent and revise based on feedback.

objectives: Reflect on growth and health goals

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the campaign to family, a co-op or community group.

days.title: Year review game
days.work: Play a review game covering nutrition, fitness, hygiene, puberty and ATOD.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Take the end-of-year health assessment.

days.title: Summer plan
days.work: Write a summer health plan with activity, sleep and hygiene goals.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on how you have grown this year and what health skill helps you most.
